chunks: Ali ibn Ibrahim, from his father, from Ibn Abi Umayr, from Hisham ibn al-Hakam, who said:
Abu Shakir al-Daysani said, “Indeed, in the Qur'an there is a verse that is our statement.” I said, “What is it?” So he said:
“And He is the One Who is God in the heaven and God in the earth.”
So I did not know how to answer him.

So I went for hajj and informed Abu Abdullah عليه السلام. He said, “This is the speech of a wicked heretic. When you return to him, say to him: ‘What is your name in al-Kufah?’ Then he will say, ‘So-and-so.’ Then say to him: ‘What is your name in al-Basrah?’ Then he will say, ‘So-and-so.’ Then say: ‘Likewise, Allah, our Lord—He is God in the heaven and God in the earth, and God in the seas, and God in the deserts, and in every place, God.’”
He said: So I returned and went to Abu Shakir and informed him. He said, “This has been transmitted from al-Hijaz.”

key_terms.آيَةً: a verse from the Qur'an cited in theological argument
key_terms.إِلٰهٌ: God; the one truly worshipped and possessing divinity
key_terms.الْحِجَازِ: the Hijaz, referring to the region from which this answer was recognized as coming
key_terms.الْقُرْآنِ: the Qur'an, the revealed scripture being discussed
key_terms.زِنْدِيقٍ: a heretic or atheist who conceals disbelief

ai.seo_question: How did Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام explain the verse 'He is God in the heaven and God in the earth'?
ai.summary: This hadith presents a reply given by Imam al-Sadiq عليه السلام to a theological objection about the verse stating that Allah is God in the heaven and in the earth. The Imam explains that this does not imply multiplicity, but affirms His divinity and authority in every place. The narration highlights a method of reasoning in defending tawhid and clarifying Qur'anic expressions.
